facts.value: A voltage applied to a human body causes an electric current through the tissues, and although the relationship is non-linear, the greater the voltage, the greater the current.

facts.value: The threshold for perception varies with the supply frequency and with the path of the current, but is about 0.1mA to 1mA for mains-frequency electricity.
facts.programme_association: Electrical Engineering - BE or ME | University of Limerick

facts.value: A current as low as a microamp can be detected as an electrovibration effect under certain conditions.
facts.programme_association: Electrical Engineering - BE or ME | University of Limerick

facts.value: If the current is sufficiently high, it will cause muscle contraction, fibrillation of the heart, and tissue burns.
facts.programme_association: Electrical Engineering - BE or ME | University of Limerick

facts.value: The lack of any visible sign that a conductor is electrified makes electricity a particular hazard.

facts.value: The pain caused by an electric shock can be intense, leading electricity at times to be employed as a method of torture.

facts.value: Death caused by an electric shock—electrocution—is still used for judicial execution in some US states, though its use had become very rare by the end of the 20th century.
